history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed: this is a Sanamahism (traditional Meitei religion) shrine, not a Hindu temple, though it is listed here per the project brief. The Sanamahi Temple (Meitei: Sanamahi Laishang / Sanamahi Sanglen) at the First Manipur Rifles Ground, Sanakhwa Yaima Kollup, near Kangla Palace in Imphal West district, is dedicated to Lainingthou Sanamahi, the supreme deity of Sanamahism. It is regarded as one of the oldest temples in Manipur/Asia and one of the largest Kanglei (Meitei-style) temples in the state; its main structures were reconstructed during the reign of Maharaja Kulachandra Singh in 1891 CE. The structure has a distinctive Gothic-style roof and an octagonal base (per Wikipedia). It is often confused with the Sanamahi Kiyong Temple on the hilltop of Nongmaiching Hill in Imphal East district - a different shrine. In Sanamahism, Sanamahi is the protector and guardian god of mankind, one of the five principal deities alongside Sidaba Mapu (creator), Pakhangba (ruler of the universe), Leimarel Sidabi (earth goddess) and Imoinu Ahongbi (goddess of wealth).

name: Sanamahi Temple
town_description: Imphal is the capital of Manipur and the historical seat of the Meitei kings. The Sanamahi Temple stands at Sanakhwa Yaima Kollup, in the First Manipur Rifles Ground near Kangla Palace (the old palace-fort) in Imphal West district - the spiritual heartland of the Meitei people and of Sanamahism, the pre-Hindu traditional religion of Manipur.
